title: Residency and KV-Cache Audit Talking Points
content:
Purpose:
Provide short, defensible talking points and seller-friendly phrasing for prospects asking about where inference data is kept, how transient caches (KV/prefix caches) are handled, and what audit logs we can provide. Target audience: AEs, CSEs, and security reviewers prepping for customer evaluations or procurement.

TL;DR (one-liners you can say on a call):
- Redwood offers configurable data residency across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — you can pin model serving to region or on-prem to meet residency requirements.
- KV/prefix caches are controlled by runtime policy — by default we don’t persist full request payloads for hosted customers; cache retention and scope are configurable for Dedicated/Private.
- We provide tamper-evident audit logs, exportable in common formats, and a BAA/ISO/SOC2 evidence bundle for enterprise evaluations.

Key claims + short proof points (sales-safe language):
1) Data residency and isolation
   - Claim: Customers can require region-bound serving and storage for inference artifacts and logs.
   - Proof point: Hosted customers may select region; Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools; Private (VPC or on-prem) places full control with the customer.
   - Evidence to offer: regional deployment manifest, Dedicated network topology, Private deployment runbook.

2) KV/prefix cache handling (common confusion area)
   - Claim: Caching is a runtime optimization that can be scoped, limited, or disabled per-customer/per-model.
   - Proof point: The serving runtime supports three configurable modes: ephemeral-only (no disk persistence), short-lived persisted cache (encrypted at rest), and long-lived caching for on-prem where customer manages storage.
   - How to answer: "We can disable persistent caching for your tenant, and we can provide a short technical note explaining how cached entries are excluded from long-term logs and how they're rotated/garbage-collected."

3) Audit logs and immutability
   - Claim: We produce structured audit logs for request lifecycle events (request arrival, routing decision, model variant used, token-level cost/latency metrics) with configurable retention and export.
   - Proof point: Logs can be pushed to customer S3 or SIEM via secure connectors; we maintain tamper-evidence controls (append-only logs with checksums) for enterprise-grade auditability.
   - Evidence to offer: sample sanitized log files, log schema doc, connector runbook.

4) Compliance posture (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA)
   - Claim: Redwood maintains SOC2 certification and is progressing ISO attestation; we support HIPAA customers via Private deployments and BAAs.
   - Proof point: SOC2 report (redacted) available under NDA; BAA template and Private deployment architecture diagram for HIPAA workloads.
   - How to answer if pressed: "For PHI, we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed keys and network isolation; our BAA outlines responsibilities and support scope."

Competitor differentiation (how to position vs cloud vendors and managed API providers):
- Versus generic cloud endpoints: Redwood provides inference-specific controls (runtime cache modes, per-tenant kernel/config profiles) and transparent per-token observability via Redwood Console.
- Versus single-mode inference vendors: Redwood is multi-mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) so customers can start with Hosted and migrate to Dedicated/Private without rewriting code or rollout policies.
- Versus open-source self-host: We deliver managed operational telemetry (traces, token-level cost) and audit evidence without the customer needing to build a telemetry stack.

Common buyer questions and sample replies (concise):
Q: Do you store prompts or user inputs?
A: For Hosted customers we retain shortened metadata and traces for debugging and billing; full request payload retention is off by default and can be configured. For Dedicated and Private, retention is customer-configurable and can be disabled.

Q: Can we get raw audit logs for every request?
A: Yes — we can provide structured, timestamped audit logs showing routing decisions, model version, duration, and token metrics. We offer export connectors to S3, GCS, or SIEMs and can provide a sample sanitized export.

Q: How do you prevent cached data leakage between tenants?
A: The runtime isolates caches by tenant and model variant. On Dedicated clusters we also enforce process-level isolation and optional CPU/GPU tenancy for extra separation.

Q: What encryption and key management controls do you provide?
A: Data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses provider-managed encryption with envelope encryption. We can discuss HSM-backed key wrapping for BAU enterprise deals.

Contract and audit-log sample language (short snippets sellers can paste into RFPs):
- "Redwood will provide append-only, time-ordered audit logs for inference requests and model routing events. Logs will be retained for a mutually agreed retention period and are exportable in JSON/CSV format to the customer's secure storage."
- "Persistent KV-cache is configurable and can be disabled for the customer's tenant; any persisted cache entries are encrypted at rest and subject to rotation policy X."
- "For processing of PHI, customer and Redwood will execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and deploy Private or Dedicated infrastructure to meet HIPAA isolation requirements."

Evidence kit (what to attach or link in an enterprise evaluation):
- Redacted SOC2 Type II report (NDA)
- Architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private deployments
- BAA template and HIPAA runbook
- Sample sanitized audit log export (1 day) and log schema
- Pen test summary and remediation tracker
- Configuration guide for disabling cache and enabling customer-managed KMS
- Redwood Console screenshots showing per-model latency and token breakdown (for SRE reviewers)

Objection handling and escalation triggers:
- If a prospect insists on immutable, 7-year retention of raw request payloads: escalate to security team; propose dedicated archival pipeline to S3 with strict access controls and legal review.
- If prospect wants per-request PII redaction: suggest client-side redaction hooks + runtime prompt transforms; involve solutions engineering for a demo.
- If prospect demands SOC2 evidence immediately: send SOC2 redacted under NDA; schedule a technical trust call within 48 hours.

Small checklist for pre-demo prep (AE/CSE):
- Confirm deployment preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and region
- Check whether prospect will process PHI or regulated data
- Prepare evidence bundle (SOC2 redacted, sample logs, BAA if HIPAA possible)
- Decide cache mode default for trial tenant and note it in onboarding checklist
- Offer a 30-minute trust call with Security + Solutions Eng for any security reviewers

Next steps and owners:
- Sales: attach this brief to outreach templates and RFP responses (owner: AE)
- Solutions Eng: prepare a one-page runbook for disabling persistent caches per-tenant (owner: Marisol)
- Security: confirm SOC2 distribution process and generate fresh sample logs for sales (owner: Ravi)

Notes / open questions to resolve (internal):
- Define exact language and retention defaults for Hosted free-tier vs paid enterprise tenants.
- Create an official sample log redaction script we can share in demos.
- Add a Dedicated checklist for verifying tenant-level encryption with customer KMS.

Quick scripts for sellers to copy into email replies (short):
- "We can restrict inference compute and logs to [region], disable persistent caching for your account, and export full audit logs to your S3 for independent archiving — happy to walk through the artifact bundle under NDA."
- "For HIPAA/PHI workloads we recommend Private deployment and a BAA; we'll provide a deployment diagram and a runbook showing where keys and logs reside."

End of doc.
